title: Configuration exceptions
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: Why is chromium different from what the rules predict?
Can you explain why copper sometimes behaves differently?
What is the general rule for writing ion configurations?

explain.say: Today we look at some exceptions to electron rules. Some elements do not follow the standard pattern.

items: Some elements break the normal pattern.
We will study specific examples today.
These exceptions are important to know.

explain.say: Chromium is a good example of an exception. Its expected configuration is different from its actual one.
Copper also shows an exception in its electron arrangement. It prefers a more stable setup.
When forming ions, we must remember to remove the highest energy electrons first. This is a key rule.
For transition metals, the stability of the resulting ion is very important. They often favor a half-filled or fully filled d-subshell.
In everyday life, understanding these exceptions helps predict chemical reactions. For example, predicting the color of a metal ion.

faq.q: Why do some elements break the standard electron rules?
faq.a: Elements sometimes rearrange electrons to achieve a more stable, lower energy state. This stability is often related to filling the d-subshell.
asks: Does stability always win over the rules?
Why do electron configurations change sometimes?

faq.q: When I write the configuration for a positive ion, which electrons do I remove?
faq.a: You must always remove the electrons from the highest principal quantum number, which is usually the 4s orbital first.
asks: Do I remove from the d or the s orbital first?
What is the order of electron removal for ions?

faq.q: What is the most stable configuration for a transition metal ion?
faq.a: The most stable configurations are those where the d-subshell is either exactly half-filled (d⁵) or completely full (d¹⁰).
asks: Are d⁵ and d¹⁰ always the most stable?

faq.q: Does the exception for chromium apply to all its compounds?
faq.a: While the ground state configuration is an exception, the stability of the ion in a compound is what matters most for prediction.
asks: How does the environment affect the configuration?

faq.q: How do I handle the copper exception when writing ion configurations?
faq.a: For copper, remember that the actual configuration is [Ar] 4s¹ 3d¹⁰, which is more stable than the expected 4s² 3d⁹.
asks: What is the correct configuration for Cu²⁺?
Should I treat Cu like a normal transition metal?

facts: Chromium has an actual configuration of [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵.
When forming positive ions, electrons are removed from the highest energy level first.
Stability is often achieved by having a half-filled (d⁵) or full (d¹⁰) d-subshell.

quiz.say: What is the most stable configuration for an ion like Nickel (Ni)?

options.show: It must follow the Aufbau principle strictly.
options.say: It must follow the Aufbau principle strictly.

options.show: It will always lose its two 4s electrons.
options.say: It will always lose its two 4s electrons.

options.show: It will adopt the configuration of the next element.
options.say: It will adopt the configuration of the next element.

options.show: It will favor a d⁸ configuration because it is close to d¹⁰.
options.say: It will favor a d⁸ configuration because it is close to d¹⁰.

quiz.why: The tendency to achieve a stable, filled d-subshell makes d⁸ a preferred state.

wrong.0: Following the Aufbau principle is the general rule, but exceptions exist for stability.
wrong.1: Losing only the 4s electrons is only correct if the resulting ion is stable.
wrong.2: The ion adopts a configuration based on its own number of electrons, not the next element.

quiz.say: If an element is expected to be [Ar] 4s² 3d⁴, but its actual configuration is [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵, which element is this?
quiz.why: This specific change from 4s² 3d⁴ to 4s¹ 3d⁵ is the defining exception for Chromium.

wrong.0: Iron's expected configuration is different from the one described.
wrong.2: Manganese is a different element with its own specific electron pattern.
wrong.3: Titanium has a different set of electrons in its outer shells.

quiz.say: When forming a cation, which orbital type should you prioritize removing electrons from first?
quiz.why: The 4s orbital is considered the highest energy level to be removed first during ionization.

wrong.0: While p orbitals are outer, the 4s orbital is the specific orbital targeted first.
wrong.2: The d orbital electrons are generally held more tightly than the 4s electrons.
wrong.3: The 3d electrons are removed only after the 4s electrons are gone.
